note: Corps of Engineers campground of the Ball Mountain Lake flood-control project, in the valley where Winhall Brook meets the West River, seven miles above the lake; the West River Trail runs past it. A narrow one-lane bridge (16-ton limit) leads to the south side. Sites near the river sit behind a brushy, wooded bank, and water held back by the dam can close parts of the campground. Cash and checks are not accepted. --Claude
summary: rec.gov description/notices/rules/rates + per-site catalog + site photos + availability: 111 sites (74 non-electric, 14 lean-to, 23 W/E 50A at S06-S28), 107 reservable, max 40 ft (stored 60), back-in. Showers, flush toilets, dump on both sides, water. $24/$28/$30. 2027 season May 21 - Oct 11 (last night Oct 10). North side open again (sites booked Aug-Oct 2026, open for May 2027). Bridge 16-ton limit (passes). WATERFRONT riverfront -> riverview recommended. Pin at the entrance station ~360 m from the first loop: move recommended. Phone matches.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored riverfront, no --AWH value) -> riverview recommended. The closest sites to water are N20-N24 (east loop with lean-tos L26-L28, ~43.1589,-72.7969) and S69-S75 (track along the West River, ~43.1556,-72.7984), both sold by the night. Esri 2024 puts them ~20-50 m from the West River (here ~35-40 m wide), but behind a strip of deciduous trees and brush on the bank; the rec.gov photos of N18-N24, N33-N36, S58-S75 all show grassy sites backed by a dense shrub and tree line with no water visible. The 23 electric sites S06-S28 ring a loop ~70-80 m from Winhall Brook behind woods. Behind a line of trees = a view; no named site is on open ground at the water.

PIN MOVE: stored 43.16297,-72.81041 (rec.gov facility point) is the entrance station/office on Winhall Station Rd, north-west of the Winhall Brook bridge. The camping loops start across the bridge: recommend ~43.1607,-72.8072 (the S06-S28 electric loop, the first loop and the middle of the south side), ~360 m from the stored pin. The campground spreads ~1.3 km to the confluence (N and S56-S75 loops at ~43.157,-72.798).
MAX LENGTH: stored 60 (derived from the old note's '30-60 ft') -> 40, the catalog's longest (97 sites at 40 ft, 14 at 30).

BRIDGE: rec.gov notice 'A narrow, one-lane bridge must be crossed to access the south side of the camping area ... The bridge weight limit is 16 tons.' Passes for an 11,000-lb rig. The old note's 42-ft vehicle limit is no longer posted; nothing on width.
